The statement signals outcome-based forward guidance at the zero lower bound and continued large-scale asset purchases ($80B Treasuries, $40B MBS), consistent with the post-1980s shift from money growth to short-term interest rate control and rule-like behavior (e.g., Taylor-type guidelines). The new average-inflation framework—seeking inflation moderately above 2% so the average returns to target—tracks the inflation-forecast-targeting literature (Svensson 1997; Svensson and Woodford 1999) and helps mitigate the classic inflation-bias problem under discretion. Balance sheet policy should ease term premia (term-structure evidence in Rudebusch and Piazzesi) and support credit via the broad credit channel (Bernanke–Blinder/Gertler), especially through MBS purchases. Acknowledging that the pandemic poses considerable risks is consistent with New Keynesian Phillips-curve dynamics and real-time uncertainty about slack (Orphanides, 2001), which strengthens the case for outcome-based guidance until “substantial further progress” is achieved. Overall tone: supportive policy credibly countering a weak demand environment and virus-related uncertainty, leaving the net assessment modestly negative but less so than before.
